title: §7.3 reserve-before-act is conditioned on the host being in host nonce mode; a local-mode host that receives consume_nonces has no textual obligation and can act without reserving
claim: §3.2 says consume_nonces is 'Emitted only in host nonce mode (§8)' and §7.3 opens 'When the host runs the verifier in host nonce mode (§8) and receives allow with consume_nonces, the host MUST reserve every entry'. Nonce mode is negotiated out-of-band (verifier CLI/config), not on the wire, so a host configured for local mode can be paired with a verifier configured for host mode (misconfiguration, or a vendor verifier that only supports host mode). Such a host reads a schema-valid allow, has no §7.3 obligation because the conditional clause does not fire, and a lazy implementer proceeds without reserving anything — while the verifier, believing it is in host mode, recorded nothing locally. The same bundle then replays indefinitely. The draft's pseudocode (`for entry in (verdict.consume_nonces or []): reserve`) implies unconditional reservation, so the two documents already diverge; the normative prose is the weaker one. Fix: state that a host MUST treat any consume_nonces it receives as binding regardless of its configured mode, and MUST deny (host-side fail-closed class, e.g. `nonce_store_unavailable`/schema_invalid) if it has no durable unique-insert store — never proceed. No current vector exercises a host driven in local/default mode with a consume_nonces allow.
evidence: spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §3.2: 'Emitted only in host nonce mode (§8). Instructs the host to durably record each one-time nonce so the same proof cannot be replayed.'

spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §7.3: 'When the host runs the verifier in **host nonce mode** (§8) and receives `allow` with `consume_nonces`, the host **MUST** reserve **every** entry in the list **before** performing the privileged a[ction]' — the MUST is inside a conditional on host mode.
spec/draft-kondoju-evc-01.md §3 pseudocode: 'for entry in (verdict.consume_nonces or []): if not reserve_nonce_atomically(entry): reject("replay")' — unconditional, contradicting the prose gating.

Conformance index (set 0.7.0): all three nonce vectors (host-nonce-reserve-novel-allow, host-nonce-reserve-replay-deny, host-nonce-reserve-all-any-conflict-deny) are described as 'in host nonce mode'; none drives the HUT without host mode enabled.
proposed_artifact: A pinned spec diff (§3.2/§7.3 + draft §7) making consume_nonces reservation unconditional on host configuration, plus a new host-behavior vector `host-nonce-consume-nonces-without-host-mode-deny-or-reserve` that runs the HUT in its default/local configuration against an allow carrying consume_nonces and requires either reserve-before-act or a fail-closed deny, never a bare proceed.

title: 'A single trailing newline is OPTIONAL' vs 'no trailing bytes': the spec never defines which bytes around the verdict object are tolerated, so RFC 8259-lenient parsers and byte-strict hosts diverge
evidence: spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §5.1: 'The verifier **MUST** write exactly one `JSON.stringify(verdict)` to the host-facing stdout, at the very end. A single trailing newline is **OPTIONAL**.'

spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §5.2: 'The host **MUST** parse the verifier's stdout as **exactly one** JSON object with **no trailing bytes**, and **MUST** reject ... stdout that is empty, not valid JSON, or contains a leading/trailing prefix or suffix around the object'

RFC 8259 §2: 'JSON-text = ws value ws' and 'Insignificant whitespace is allowed before or after any of the six structural characters' (https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8259#section-2) — JSON.parse and serde_json accept surrounding whitespace by default.

Conformance index (set 0.7.0): host-deny-allow-trailing-garbage ('followed by trailing garbage') and host-deny-leading-garbage ('a non-JSON PREFIX') are the only framing vectors; no vector uses CRLF, leading whitespace, or multiple LFs.
proposed_artifact: A pinned spec diff adding an explicit stdout framing grammar to §5.1/§5.2 (and draft §4.4), plus two vectors — `host-allow-trailing-crlf-and-leading-whitespace` (positive control for RFC 8259 whitespace) and `host-deny-trailing-nul-after-newline` (non-whitespace suffix) — so a host cannot pass the suite as either an over-strict or an over-lenient framer.

title: 'oversized stdout' is a host fail-closed condition and the first-precedence classification, yet no verdict size limit is defined anywhere; a host can pick any bound and still pass host-deny-oversize-stdout
claim: §7.2 lists 'unparseable, empty, oversized, or multi-object stdout (§5.2)' as deny conditions and ranks 'output bound' first in the classification precedence, but §5.2 never mentions size and §6 bounds only stdin ('The verifier MUST bound the request read from stdin ... 1 MiB'). There is no maximum a verifier may emit and no minimum a host must accept. A lazy host sets its output bound at, say, 512 bytes: it passes host-deny-oversize-stdout (which only requires rejecting a flood 'past the host's output bound') while misclassifying every legitimate deny that carries a §3.3 `detail` object with echoed sdk_code/trace context — or an allow with several human+agent consume_nonces entries at ~80 decimal digits each — as output_bound_exceeded instead of relaying it. Conversely a verifier has no rule against emitting a multi-megabyte `detail`, which a pipe-draining host with wait()-before-read will deadlock on until timeout. Fix: specify a verifier MUST NOT emit a verdict exceeding N bytes (RECOMMENDED 64 KiB, chosen to fit a single pipe buffer on common platforms) and a host MUST accept verdicts up to at least N before classifying as oversized; state that `message` is single-line and bounded.
evidence: spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §7.2: 'unparseable, empty, oversized, or multi-object stdout (§5.2)' and 'classify the cause it acted on in this precedence: its own kills first (output bound, then timeout)' — §5.2 contains no size rule.
spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §6: only 'stdin bound. The verifier **MUST** bound the request read from stdin. The reference limit is **1 MiB**' — no stdout/verdict bound is stated.

spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §3.3: '`detail` (object, **OPTIONAL**) — structured context for logs/debugging. A verifier **SHOULD** echo the originating internal error code here' — unbounded object, so verdict size is verifier-controlled.

Conformance index (set 0.7.0): host-deny-oversize-stdout — 'the verifier floods stdout past the host's output bound' — the bound is the HUT's own, not a pinned value, so any bound including a tiny one passes.
proposed_artifact: A pinned spec diff adding a normative verdict size ceiling for verifiers and a minimum acceptance floor for hosts (§5.1/§5.2/§6, mirrored in draft §4.4), plus a positive-control vector `host-relay-deny-with-large-detail` (a schema-valid deny with a multi-KiB detail object well under the floor) that a host with an undersized output bound fails.

title: `retain_until: 4102444800.0` or `4.1024448e9` — JSON Schema 'integer' admits zero-fraction floats, JS Number.isInteger agrees, serde i64 rejects; the two reference-host stacks diverge and no vector pins it
claim: §3.4 declares `retain_until` (and the request's `now_unix`/`version`) as `"type": "integer"`. Under JSON Schema 2020-12 an integer is any number with a zero fractional part, so `4102444800.0` and `4.1024448e9` are schema-valid; a JS host using Number.isInteger (or Ajv) accepts them and stores retain_until, while a Rust host deserializing into i64/u64 rejects the token and fails closed as schema_invalid. Both pass every current vector: host-deny-nonce-entry-wrong-type covers a non-numeric type, not a float-lexical integer. The divergence is not merely cosmetic — a host that accepts `retain_until: 1e400` (JS parses to Infinity, Number.isInteger(Infinity) is false, so it denies) versus `retain_until: 9007199254740993` (JS silently rounds to 2^53, Rust keeps it exact) yields different retention horizons across hosts for the same verdict bytes. The same question applies verifier-side to `version: 1.0` (schema `const: 1` matches 1.0 under JSON equality) and `now_unix: 1751990400.0`. Fix: pin the wire lexical form — integers MUST be serialized as JSON int literals (no fraction, no exponent), MUST fit in [0, 2^53-1] (I-JSON RFC 7493 §2.2 precision), and a host MUST treat any other numeric lexeme as schema-invalid.
evidence: spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §3.4 verdict schema: '"retain_until": { "type": "integer" }' and §2.2 request schema '"version": { "type": "integer", "const": 1 }', '"now_unix": { "type": "integer", "exclusiveMinimum": 0 }'.

JSON Schema Validation 2020-12 §6.1.1: type 'integer' matches 'any number with a zero fractional part' (https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/json-schema-validation#section-6.1.1) — so 1.0 and 1e9 validate as integers.
RFC 7493 (I-JSON) §2.2: numbers beyond IEEE 754 double precision are not interoperable; recommends integer values within [-(2**53)+1, (2**53)-1] (https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7493#section-2.2).

Runnable divergence check: `node -e 'console.log(Number.isInteger(JSON.parse("4102444800.0")))'` prints true; `echo '4102444800.0' | cargo script`-equivalent `serde_json::from_str::<i64>("4102444800.0")` returns Err("invalid type: floating point `4102444800.0`, expected i64").
Conformance index (set 0.7.0): host-deny-nonce-entry-wrong-type — 'an allow whose nonce entry has a s[tring]...' — covers type mismatch only; no vector sends a float-lexical or exponent-form integer.
proposed_artifact: Two new host-behavior vectors — `host-deny-nonce-entry-retain-until-float-lexical` (retain_until: 4102444800.0) and `host-deny-nonce-entry-retain-until-exponent-lexical` (retain_until: 4.1024448e9) — with expected `schema_invalid`, plus a pinned spec diff to §3.4/§2.2 (and draft schemas appendix) stating integer fields MUST be JSON int literals within the I-JSON safe range.

title: Timeout kill of the verifier parent leaves the fd-3 worker (and any grandchild) alive: late nonce burn + lingering verification of a denied request
claim: §7.2 obligates the host to 'kill the process and deny' on timeout, but §5.1 makes the reference verifier a two-process design (parent + worker on fd 3). 'The process' is singular and unqualified: a host that sends SIGKILL to the direct child PID only (the naive spawn/kill idiom in Node, Rust std, Python subprocess) leaves the worker running with the full request in memory. Attack/consequence: in local nonce mode the orphaned worker can finish verification and durably burn the presentation's nullifier AFTER the host has already denied, so the legitimate retry of the same presentation is rejected `nonce_replayed`; an attacker who can induce slow verification (large but under-bound bundle, many Groth16 verifies) turns every timeout into a one-shot burn of the victim agent's nonce. Secondarily, orphaned workers accumulate across timeouts (resource exhaustion) and any grandchild holding the inherited stdout write end can keep the host's read-until-EOF loop open. No vector in set 0.7.0 observes process-tree state after the host's timeout kill (host-deny-no-output-timeout and host-deny-partial-json-timeout only assert the deny/classification).
evidence: §7.2 (pinned 9bf7544): 'timeout (§6) — the host **MUST** kill the process and deny;' — singular 'the process', no mention of the process group, session, or descendants.

§5.1 (pinned 9bf7544): 'the command **spawns a worker** process that performs the entire verification; the worker's stdio binds fd 0 = request in, **fd 1 = captured** ... **fd 3 = the private verdict channel**' — the reference verifier is by construction a parent+worker pair, so a PID-only kill provably leaves the verifier that is actually doing the work running.

Runnable: `git show 9bf754441ab36ab93992ed5936d34c44a4128f92:spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md | grep -n -i 'process group\|descendant\|orphan\|setsid\|killpg'` returns no matches; `git show 9bf754441ab36ab93992ed5936d34c44a4128f92:spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md | grep -n 'kill the process'` shows the singular obligation.

Vector index (set 0.7.0, 29 vectors) — the two timeout vectors 'host-deny-no-output-timeout' and 'host-deny-partial-json-timeout' assert the verdict outcome only; none describes an assertion over the verifier's process tree after the kill.

Registry §9 (pinned): 'nonce_replayed | the proof's one-time nonce was already seen (local mode)' — the local-mode burn is durable, so a post-deny burn by an orphan is user-visible on the next honest presentation.
proposed_artifact: Staged spec diff to §6/§7.2 (host MUST terminate the verifier's entire process tree on timeout — process group/job object — and MUST NOT act until the tree is reaped) plus a new host_behavior vector `host-deny-timeout-kills-verifier-tree` whose fixture parent spawns a grandchild that sleeps past the deadline and then writes a sentinel file; the runner asserts deny with class timeout AND that the sentinel is absent after the HUT returns.

title: In host nonce mode a bare `allow` (no consume_nonces) is indistinguishable from 'verifier did no replay check' — silent loss of replay protection on mode mismatch
claim: §3.2 says `consume_nonces` 'is omitted entirely when there is nothing to burn', so a bare `{"verdict":"allow"}` is a legal host-mode verdict and the host proceeds without reserving anything. But the same bare `allow` is exactly what a verifier emits when it (a) ignored or never implemented the host-mode switch, (b) is a `classical`/`external`-class verifier with no nonce concept, or (c) ran in local mode against an empty/ephemeral store. The host cannot tell these apart: the verdict carries no confirmation of which nonce mode produced it, the schema is closed (additionalProperties:false) so a verifier cannot add one, and `kind` is explicitly non-authoritative. Attack: an operator configures host nonce mode expecting the host's durable store to be the replay barrier, spawns a verifier that answers bare allows, and every presentation is replayable for the whole credential lifetime with zero deny signals. This is a fail-open-by-configuration path that the fail-closed rules in §7.2 do not cover, and it contradicts the registry's own `nonce_missing` row (a proof with no usable nullifier is supposed to be a deny, not an allow-with-nothing-to-burn).
evidence: §3.2 (pinned 9bf7544): '`consume_nonces` (array of objects, **OPTIONAL**, allow-only). When present it is a **non-empty** list (the key is omitted entirely when there is nothing to burn).'

§9 registry (pinned): 'nonce_missing | the proof lacks a usable nullifier / session-nonce signal.' and 'nonce_replayed | ... (local mode).' — the spec has no row or rule for 'host mode, verifier returned allow with no nonces'.

§3.5 (pinned): 'The value is **self-reported by the verifier and is not authenticated**' and 'a host **MUST NOT** use it to relax trust, verifier selection, schema validation, nonce handling' — so `kind` cannot be the host's signal that replay protection happened.
§3.4 allow schema (pinned): `"additionalProperties": false` with only `verdict`, `kind`, `consume_nonces` — no field can carry a nonce-mode acknowledgement within wire major 1.

Runnable: `git show 9bf754441ab36ab93992ed5936d34c44a4128f92:spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md | grep -n 'nothing to burn\|host nonce mode'` — shows the omission rule and the mode text; no line couples them.

Vector index (set 0.7.0): the three nonce vectors (host-nonce-reserve-novel-allow, host-nonce-reserve-replay-deny, host-nonce-reserve-all-any-conflict-deny) all carry consume_nonces; no vector exercises a bare allow while the HUT is in host nonce mode.
proposed_artifact: Staged spec diff adding a host obligation to §7.3/§8: a host in host nonce mode MUST treat an `allow` without `consume_nonces` as fail-closed (`schema_invalid`/`nonce_missing` classification) unless it is explicitly configured to accept nonce-less presentations, plus a new vector `host-nonce-mode-bare-allow-deny` (host nonce mode, well-formed bare allow at exit 0, expected deny) and a matching verifier obligation that host-mode verifiers MUST deny `nonce_missing` rather than emit a nonce-less allow.

title: No rule ties `retain_until` to credential expiry: a reservation evicted before `effective_expiry` reopens replay for the remaining lifetime (refines the iteration-5 retain_until candidate with a single well-formed hunk)
claim: Refinement of the iteration-5 candidate that was dropped for invalid diff syntax, not for substance. §3.2 makes `retain_until` REQUIRED and says the host MUST retain the nonce until that time, but nothing constrains its value: it may be less than `now_unix`, or less than the credential's `effective_expiry`. Because §9 defines expiry as strict `now_unix >= effective_expiry`, the proof remains acceptable for every second in (retain_until, effective_expiry). A host that honors the spec literally evicts at `retain_until`, after which the identical bundle re-presents with the identical `consume_nonces` and reserves cleanly — replay with no deny signal. Binding v2 signs `expiry` so the presenter cannot move expiry, but the verifier chooses `retain_until` unilaterally and the host has no obligation to sanity-check it. The fix needs two obligations: verifier `retain_until` MUST be >= the credential's effective expiry, and the host MUST fail closed on `retain_until <= now_unix` (a retention window that has already ended makes reserve-before-act vacuous).
evidence: §3.2 (pinned 9bf7544): '`retain_until` (integer, **REQUIRED**) — Unix seconds until which the host **MUST** retain the consumed nonce.' — no lower bound relative to `now_unix` or expiry.
§3.4 schema (pinned): `"retain_until": { "type": "integer" }` — no minimum at all; `0` and negative values are schema-valid.

§9 registry (pinned): 'expired | proof-anchored `now_unix >= effective_expiry` — a strict comparison; the equality boundary is rejected.' — establishes that the proof is live for all `now_unix < effective_expiry`, i.e. after an early eviction.

§4.1 (pinned): 'a verifier **MUST** additionally require `binding.expiry == credential.expiry`' — expiry is signature-bound (v2), so the only unbound liveness parameter left in the replay path is `retain_until`.
Runnable: `git show 9bf754441ab36ab93992ed5936d34c44a4128f92:spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md | grep -n 'retain_until'` — every occurrence is a definition; none is a bound.

Previous iteration record: experiment `security-researcher-retain-until-schema-unbounded-relative-to-now-unix` dropped_acceptance with finding 'section-label hunk headers are invalid unified-diff syntax, and the embedded schema fence prematurely closes the diff block' — formatting, not substance.
proposed_artifact: Staged spec diff (one prose hunk to §3.2 and one schema hunk to §3.4, both with real `@@ -l,c +l,c @@` headers and no nested fences) adding (a) verifier obligation `retain_until >= effective_expiry` and (b) host obligation to fail closed on `retain_until <= now_unix`, plus a new host_behavior vector `host-deny-retain-until-not-in-future` (allow with a nonce entry whose `retain_until` is 1) expected to deny with classification `schema_invalid`.

title: Reserve-before-act is not ordered after full verdict validation: a host may durably burn nonce[0] before discovering nonce[1] is schema-invalid, so a verifier bug consumes a valid one-time nonce without any action taken
claim: §7.3 says reserve EVERY entry before acting and §7.2 says a verdict failing the §3.4 schema is a deny, but the spec never states that schema validation of the whole verdict MUST complete before the first reservation. A streaming or entry-by-entry host (validate entry, reserve entry, next) reserves nonce[0] with unique-insert semantics, then hits a malformed nonce[1] (missing `retain_until`, wrong type, extra property) and denies — leaving nonce[0] permanently burned for a presentation that never executed. Attack: any party who can make the verifier emit a partially malformed multi-nonce allow (or simply a verifier regression) turns a schema deny into a permanent burn of the agent's nullifier and, for human-backed bundles, the `human:<nullifierHash>` entry — the honest re-presentation then fails as replay. The existing vectors host-deny-malformed-consume-nonce, host-deny-nonce-entry-wrong-type and host-deny-nonce-entry-extra-property assert only the deny; none observes the nonce store afterwards, so an entry-by-entry host passes the suite.
evidence: §7.3 (pinned 9bf7544): 'the host **MUST** reserve **every** entry in the list **before** performing the privileged a[ction]' — orders reservation before action, not validation before reservation.

§7.2 (pinned): host MUST deny 'a verdict that otherwise fails the §3.4 verdict schema — including ... a `code` outside the §9 registry, or any disallowed additional property.' — separate obligation, no ordering relative to §7.3.

§3.2 (pinned): 'A presentation can carry more than one nonce to reserve — e.g. the agent nullifier **plus** a human-uniqueness nullifier when the bundle is human-backed' — multi-entry lists are the normal case for human-backed bundles, so partial reservation is a realistic path.

Runnable: `git show 9bf754441ab36ab93992ed5936d34c44a4128f92:spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md | grep -n -i 'before reserving\|prior to reserv\|validate.*before'` returns nothing ordering validation ahead of reservation.

Vector index (set 0.7.0): 'host-deny-malformed-consume-nonce: ... an `allow` whose `consume_nonces` entry omits the REQU[IRED field]', 'host-deny-nonce-entry-wrong-type', 'host-deny-nonce-entry-extra-property' — all described as deny assertions; 'host-nonce-reserve-novel-allow' is the only vector whose description implies store inspection, and it is the positive case.

Runnable conformance baseline: `npx @bolyra/evc-conformance@0.3.0 --host "<cmd>"` — an entry-by-entry HUT passes all three malformed-nonce vectors today because the store is never inspected on the deny path.
proposed_artifact: A new host_behavior vector `host-deny-malformed-second-nonce-no-partial-reserve`: an allow with nonce[0] valid and nonce[1] missing `retain_until`; the runner asserts deny with class `schema_invalid` AND, using the same nonce-store env convention as host-nonce-reserve-replay-deny, that nonce[0] is NOT present in the store after the run — plus a one-sentence §7.3 clarification that the complete verdict MUST validate against §3.4 before any entry is reserved.

title: EVC admits a capability class, not an action instance; request extension fields are silently unbound
claim: Every competing pre-action layer decides per tool call with its arguments in scope: OAP (arXiv 2603.20953) 'intercepts tool calls synchronously before execution, evaluates them against a declarative policy'; agentgateway evaluates CEL rules 'against method invocations such as list_tools and call_tools'; Pomerium's mcp_tool criterion gates 'per-tool allow/deny on every request'. EVC's request carries only agent_name/project_key/program/model/granted_capabilities, and the binding v2 signs exactly six fields, none of which is a tool name or an argument digest. Worse, both the envelope and the inner request object are declared additionalProperties: true while no verifier obligation exists to reject or even acknowledge unknown request fields. A host that adds e.g. tool_args_sha256 to request and receives allow has no way to know the verifier never looked at it: extension fields create a fail-open belief without a fail-closed rule. EVC should state that (a) the decision is a capability-class admission unless the action instance is folded into a granted_capabilities token so it is covered by the signed binding, and (b) request extension fields are not authorization inputs unless a verifier's documented contract says so, so hosts MUST NOT assume they were verified.
evidence: spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §2.2 request schema: `"additionalProperties": true` on the envelope and again on the inner `request` object; no verifier MUST governs unknown request fields anywhere in §2

spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §2.1: `granted_capabilities` are 'host-defined capability tokens the host intends to grant. They are opaque strings that the verifier maps to its internal permission model' — no tool name or argument field exists

spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §4.1: 'Let `binding` be the object with exactly the six fields `agent_name`, `project_key`, `program`, `model`, `capabilities` (a string array), and `expiry`' — the signed surface cannot bind an action instance
https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.20953 — OAP 'intercepts tool calls synchronously before execution, evaluates them against a declarative policy, and produces a cryptographically signed audit record'
https://agentgateway.dev/docs/standalone/main/mcp/mcp-authz/ — CEL rules evaluated against `call_tools` invocations; hidden-tool calls rejected with an authorization error
https://www.pomerium.com/blog/top-5-agentic-gateways-for-securing-mcp-tool-calls-in-2026 — `mcp_tool` criterion for per-tool allow/deny on every request
proposed_artifact: A staged prose-only diff (wire unchanged) to §2.1/§2.2 and the -02 draft request section adding a normative 'extension fields are not authorization inputs' rule for hosts and verifiers, plus an informative 'action-instance binding' note showing the capability-token fold so the tool/argument instance lands inside the signed binding.

title: No host-conformance vector exercises the deny `detail` object — EVC's only channel for step-up hints
claim: AuthZEN COAZ/AARP (tracked threat card) carry a third 'prerequisite pending' outcome and draft-klrc-aiagent-auth-03 models step-up/consent as first-class flows. EVC's closed two-outcome verdict and closed 15-code registry mean a verifier wanting to say 'obtainable after consent' can only stuff hints (retry_after, step_up_url) into the OPTIONAL `detail` object under an existing code. That makes `detail` the load-bearing extensibility surface for admission semantics, yet across all 29 vectors in set 0.7.0 none sends a deny that carries `detail` at all. Two host behaviours are therefore unproven: (1) positive control — a schema-valid deny with a nested `detail` object (including adversarial nested keys such as `"verdict":"allow"` or `"consume_nonces":[]` inside detail) MUST be relayed as that deny, neither rejected as schema_invalid nor upgraded; (2) negative — a deny whose `detail` is a non-object (string/array/null) fails the §3.4 schema and MUST fail closed as schema_invalid. A host that never saw a detail-bearing deny can pass 29/29 while either dropping conforming denies or, worse, letting a nested field reach its allow path.
evidence: spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §3.3: '`detail` (object, **OPTIONAL**) — structured context for logs/debugging. A verifier **SHOULD** echo the originating internal error code here'

spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §3.4 deny schema: `"detail": { "type": "object" }` inside an `"additionalProperties": false` object — a non-object `detail` is a schema failure, an object with arbitrary nested content is valid

spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §7.2: the host MUST treat as deny 'a verdict that otherwise fails the §3.4 verdict schema'; §3.5: the host 'MUST NOT upgrade a `deny` to an `allow`' on any advisory field
Conformance vector index (set 0.7.0, 29 host_behavior vectors): the only deny relay control is host-relay-well-behaved-deny (`deny code=expired`); no listed vector description mentions `detail`

threat_board.json card ecosystem-scout-authzen-coaz-aarp-mcp-decision-envelope: AuthZEN drafts 'define a competing decision envelope for MCP tool authorization with a third prerequisite pending outcome'
proposed_artifact: Two staged host-conformance vectors in the existing fixture format — host-relay-deny-with-detail-object (positive control with adversarial nested keys, expected relay of the outer deny code) and host-deny-deny-detail-wrong-type (expected failure_class schema_invalid) — with APPLY.md covering scripts/sync.js and golden regeneration.

title: OAP signs every decision; EVC's verdict is an unauthenticated stdout blob with no defined decision-record tuple
claim: OAP's headline property is that each pre-action decision 'produces a cryptographically signed audit record' and CONTINUITY (arXiv 2609.05269) requires 'every realized external effect to be backed by a valid authorization witness'. EVC's verdict is one unsigned JSON object on stdout; `kind` is explicitly 'self-reported by the verifier and is not authenticated', and the draft's exclusions list never addresses audit. Bolyra ships hash-chained ES256K receipts, but neither the spec nor the -01 draft says what a host's record of an EVC decision must bind to, so two hosts recording the 'same' decision will disagree and a skeptical third party cannot re-run it. The competing specs win this argument today. EVC can close it without a wire change: define the minimal reproducible decision-record tuple — configured verifier identity (command + argv), digest of the exact request bytes written to stdin, digest of the exact stdout bytes, exit status or signal, the §16.3 failure class the host acted on, now_unix, and the nonces reserved — such that a third party holding the tuple can re-spawn the verifier and obtain byte-identical stdout. That is also exactly the shape the loop's own evidence ledger demands (pinned commit + command).

title: The denial-code and `kind` vocabularies are declared closed within a wire major, which is incompatible with an RFC 8126 IANA registry unless the registry carries a wire-major column and a matching registration policy
claim: §4.2 of the draft says the 15-code table 'is the candidate IANA registry' and simultaneously that codes cannot be added, removed or renamed without a wire-major bump, and that a host MUST fail closed on any out-of-table code. An IANA registry exists precisely so values can be added without republishing the spec; as written, any registration would immediately make every conforming host reject the newly registered code, so the IANA Considerations section as a plain registry is self-contradictory and an IESG/IANA reviewer will bounce it. Resolution text for the IANA section: (1) name the registry 'EVC Verdict Denial Codes' with columns Code, Wire Major, Description, Reference; (2) registration policy 'Specification Required' (RFC 8126 §4.6) with the additional rule that a new code MUST be registered under a new wire-major value and MUST NOT be added to an existing major's row set, making the per-major closure explicit; (3) initial contents = the 15 codes at major 1; (4) a second registry 'EVC Verifier Proof-System Classes' for `kind` with initial contents classical/zk/external under the same per-major rule, since §5 also makes that set closed; (5) change controller IETF. Without a `kind` registry the draft has a second closed enum with no registration path at all.
evidence: spec/draft-kondoju-evc-01.md §4.2 (pinned 9bf754441ab36ab93992ed5936d34c44a4128f92): "Within a wire major, this registry is closed: the deny schema ({{schemas}}) enumerates exactly these codes, so a verdict carrying any other "code" fails the verdict schema and the host MUST fail closed"

spec/draft-kondoju-evc-01.md §4.2: "Verifiers MUST NOT add, remove, or rename a code without a wire-major version bump ({{versioning}}). ... This 15-code table is the candidate IANA registry ({{iana}})."

spec/draft-kondoju-evc-01.md §5: ""kind" takes exactly one of three values ... A verifier MUST NOT emit a "kind" value outside the three-member set above; a host MUST treat an unrecognized "kind" as a malformed verdict and fail closed"

RFC 8126 §4 (https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8126#section-4): each registry must state a registration policy; §4.6 defines Specification Required; §2.2 requires initial contents and the registry name to be stated in IANA Considerations.

Conformance vector `host-deny-unknown-denial-code` (set 0.7.0) already enforces host rejection of any non-table code, so a registry addition without a major bump would break every conforming host — the closure rule is load-bearing and must be encoded in the registration policy, not left implicit.
proposed_artifact: A staged diff replacing the draft's IANA Considerations section with two RFC 8126-formatted registry definitions (denial codes, proof-system classes) that carry a Wire Major column and a Specification-Required-plus-new-major policy, plus a cross-reference sentence in §4.2 and §5, pinned to 9bf7544.

title: Independent-verifier record: a from-spec §4 reimplementation (Node crypto only) accepts a mandate minted by the shipped `bolyra mandate issue` signer
claim: Every binding-v2 claim in the ledger today is self-referential: the reference signer and the reference verifier share the same canonicalize/DST/digest code. A skeptical third party would demand that a verifier written only from the spec text of §4.1–§4.4 — sorted-key compact JSON, DST 'bolyra.external-verifier.binding.v2' || 0x00 || payload, SHA-256, reduction mod BN254 order, EdDSA-Poseidon verify against the operator public key — accepts a bundle minted by the shipped signer, and rejects the same bundle with a five-field (no expiry) binding as unsupported_version. Restricting the test binding to ASCII-only field values sidesteps the lone-surrogate canonicalization divergence that sank the iteration-5 hostile-implementer candidate, so this record substantiates spec-conformance of the signer without asserting anything about canonicalizer edge cases.
evidence: Spec §4.1 (pinned 9bf754441ab36ab93992ed5936d34c44a4128f92): 'Let binding be the object with exactly the six fields agent_name, project_key, program, model, capabilities (a string array), and expiry ... payload = canonicalize(binding)'; §4.2: 'DST = utf8("bolyra.external-verifier.binding.v2") dsInput = DST || 0x00 || payload'; §4.3: 'digest = SHA-256(dsInput) ... msgField = BigInt("0x" || hex(digest)) mod BN254_FIELD_ORDER' with the order 21888242871839275222246405745257275088548364400416034343698204186575808495617 quoted verbatim.

Spec §4.4: 'Verify: recompute msgField from the bundle's own binding bytes, then EdDSA-Poseidon-verify sig against the operator public key that the proof commits to.' and §4.1: 'A verifier MUST reject a binding that omits expiry with deny code=unsupported_version'.

CLAUDE.md: 'Mint mandates with bolyra mandate issue (integrations/cli/src/commands/mandate-issue.ts) — issuance only, not a wallet' and 'The MPP gate, bolyra verify, and hosted-verify pin the same byte-compatible binding digest/vector'.

Iteration-5 rejection of hostile-implementer-canonicalize-defined-by-package-not-algorithm: 'the pinned canonicalizer serializes lone surrogates and the binding parser permits them' — the reason this record confines itself to ASCII-only bindings and makes no claim about surrogate handling.

Procedure (all local, no network): (1) at the pinned commit build the CLI and mint one mandate with `bolyra mandate issue` using flags taken verbatim from integrations/cli/src/commands/mandate-issue.ts (Tier 2 resolves the exact flags from the pinned source; the objective check fails if any flag is a placeholder); (2) a standalone script under standards-autoresearch/ using only node:crypto for SHA-256 and the BabyJubjub EdDSA-Poseidon verify primitive for the curve check, taking the bundle's binding bytes and signature as input; expected output: `verify=true` for the six-field binding and `deny code=unsupported_version` for the same binding with expiry removed; (3) `bolyra verify` on the same bundle; expected: allow (exit 0) — the two acceptances must agree.
proposed_artifact: A ledger entry of kind interop_run (rfc7942_ready: true) plus the from-spec verifier script and its recorded output, substantiating 'a verifier implemented from §4 text alone, sharing no code with the signer, accepts the reference signer's binding-v2 output and rejects binding v1'.

title: Discriminative-power record: run the two newest vectors against the JS reference host as it existed before each vector landed, to show the vector actually fails a host that lacks the behavior
claim: A conformance suite where every vector has only ever been observed passing proves nothing to a skeptic; the VATE-#57 pattern demands a negative control. The two vectors added since set 0.6.0 (host-deny-unknown-denial-code, host-deny-signal-death-after-allow) should be run against spec/reference-host.js at the parent of the commit that introduced each vector. The outcome is recorded whichever way it falls: a FAIL at the pre-vector commit demonstrates the vector discriminates; a PASS means the reference host already behaved correctly and the vector's discriminative power must instead be shown against a deliberately lenient host, which becomes a vector_gap for the next iteration. This replaces the iteration-5 'delta record' that was dropped for asserting an unverified delta.
evidence: Iteration-5 rejection of evidence-curator-external-impl-27-to-29-delta-record-khandrew1: 'commit 030884b introduced both the implementation listing and host-deny-unknown-denial-code' — establishes that 030884b is the introducing commit for that vector, so `030884b~1` is the pre-vector state.

Recent commit 9bf7544 'spec: host-deny-signal-death-after-allow vector — set 0.7.0, evc-conformance 0.3.0 (#126)' — the introducing commit for the second vector, so `9bf7544~1` is its pre-vector state.

Spec §9-equivalent registry closure text (draft-kondoju-evc-01 §4.2): 'A host MUST NOT relay an unrecognized "code" as if it were a valid verifier decision ... the deny is the host's fail-closed override, never a relayed verdict' — the behavior host-deny-unknown-denial-code tests; a pre-fix host that relays the code passes the deny-outcome check but must fail the classification check (schema_invalid).

Procedure (isolated scratch workspace, per iteration-1 calibration; no outbound): `git clone --no-hardlinks <local repo path> /tmp/evc-negctl && cd /tmp/evc-negctl`; then for each pair (vector, commit): `git checkout <commit>~1 -- spec/reference-host.js`, restore the current runner and fixtures with `git checkout 9bf754441ab36ab93992ed5936d34c44a4128f92 -- spec/conformance-runner.js spec/fixtures/host-conformance`, run `node spec/conformance-runner.js --host "node spec/reference-host.js"`, and record only the two named vectors' PASS/FAIL lines and the reported classification. Expected: outcome recorded as observed; the record makes no prediction.

Rule 2a compliance: the loop itself writes nothing outside standards-autoresearch/; the checkout sequence is the founder's or a third party's reproduction in a throwaway clone, and the shipped-context note that host-deny-signal-death-after-allow is already shipped is respected — the vector is not re-proposed, only its discriminative power is measured.
proposed_artifact: A ledger entry of kind interop_run (rfc7942_ready: false, negative control) with the pre-vector commit, the exact vector-by-vector observed outcome, and either a 'discriminates' conclusion or a follow-on vector_gap candidate for a deliberately lenient host fixture.
